rationale: The run produced the regression underlying Figure 6 in results/unemployment_cross_section.json under avg_urate_vs_empgrowth: slope = -33.31, t = -1.71, r2 = 0.056, n = 51, over window '1976-1990'. The paper reports slope -0.06 with t-stat 0.04 (essentially no relationship) over 1970-90. Neither number matches: the slope differs by orders of magnitude (partly a units/orientation difference, since the plan regresses average unemployment ON average employment growth), and — more tellingly — the t-statistic, which is invariant to regression orientation in a simple bivariate fit, is -1.71 here versus 0.04 in the paper, i.e. this run finds a weakly negative (though still non-significant) relationship rather than the paper's essentially null one. Both values fall far outside the match/partial bands. The deviation traces to a data-coverage limitation documented in notes/unemployment_notes.md: LAUS reconstructs state unemployment only for 1976-1990, so the intended 1970-90 window could not be reproduced. No figure6.pdf was emitted (figures/ contains no fig6 output), but the numeric regression evidence exists and is gradeable. fix_severity.json shows no fix touching this specific regression path.
